gap: No result ChatGPT got lays the 1 kWh field side by side with today's price and the load each maker's noise figure covers. Only the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 states a figure for a fridge-level discharge band (0-20 dB under 200 W). EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Plus ($649) and DELTA 3 Classic ($459) state theirs at 600 W. BLUETTI's Elite 100 V2 ($499) says 30 dB under light loads. BLUETTI's AC180 ($549, out of stock until late November) publishes no dB figure. Jackery's 1000 v2 figure covers quiet charging only.
standout_why: I compared five pages. thepowerstationguide.com (cited) has a dB table but no prices and no fan-off wattage. powerstationgeek.com noise ratings (cited) lists 27 sustained-load dB readings, among them 41 dB for the DELTA 3 Plus, but no prices and no low-load condition. powerstationadvisor.com (cited) gives no model dB figures and no prices. testedwatts.com (cited) gives the Anker and EcoFlow claims but says outright that it lists no prices. portable-powerstation.co.uk (cited) calls the C1000 Gen 2 'near-silent' at light load, with no dB figure and no price. quiettechreport.com and beacar.com also lack prices and fan-start wattages. None of these pages names the Elite 100 V2's light-load claim or the AC180 stock-out. Our own quietest-1000wh page has some prices but no fridge-level discharge figure except Anker's.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pick, the Anker C1000 Gen 2, as the only 1 kWh unit whose maker publishes a noise figure for the under-200 W band where a fridge sits. It also gives the cheaper fallbacks with a priced reason each loses: Elite 100 V2 ($499) states only a looser 30 dB 'light load' claim; DELTA 3 Classic ($459) and DELTA 3 Plus ($649) state theirs at 600 W, and Power Station Geek measured the Plus at 41 dB under sustained load; AC180 ($549) publishes no figure and is out of stock until late November. No source gives a measured fan-on wattage for any of them, so the pick rests on maker claims, not a test.

findings.label: maker noise claim, discharge
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C Series | Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Exact text: 'When discharging under 200W, C1000 Gen 2 runs at an ultra-quiet 0-20 dB.' It is the only maker figure in this field stated for a sub-200 W discharge band, where a fridge's 50-150 W compressor draw falls. No distance is stated. The product page (ankersolix.com/products/c1000-gen2) shows only '20dB Operation' with no condition.

findings.label: Notebookcheck measured noise
findings.value: about 45 dB at 1 m under high output or fast AC charging; 'much quieter to silent' at lower load
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 im Praxis-Test
findings.note: German text: 'mit gut 45 dB (aus 1 m Entfernung gemessen)'; 'Bei geringerer Last ist sie deutlich leiser bis lautlos.' No wattage is given for when the fan stops.

findings.label: MacRumors on fan noise
findings.value: fans loud at about 1,200 W charging; 'near silent' when charging small devices

findings.note: Where it loses: MacRumors wrote 'I wouldn't be able to sleep with the fans on that high' about fast charging. So if the station is also recharging from the wall overnight, the fridge-load claim no longer applies.
